SAR: If a mission is related to a specific incident and that incident has a priority level of 'high', then the mission should also be assigned as a 'high' priority.
If an incident is identified and a vulnerable object is also identified, then it can be inferred that the vulnerable object is involved in that incident.

If an incident is involved within a dataset, and that dataset was produced by a task and that task is related with a media item, then the location of incident is the same with the location of media item.
If an incident has an impact, and that impact affects a vulnerable object, then the incident's severity level is classified as 'high'.

If a responder is assigned to a mission, and that mission is related to an incident and the location of the incident is known, then the location of responder is the same with the location of the incident.

If an incident is detected and the confidence of this detection is greater than 0.9 and vulnerable objects are also detected, then the priority of the incident is set to 'high' and the detected vulnerable objects are involved in this incident.
If a measurement of a climate parameter is taken at a specific location, and an incident occurs at that same location, then that measurement can be associated with that incident.
If a detection has a start time and an end time, and its total duration is calculated to be greater than 60 minutes, then the severity of the incident is 'high'.
If a vulnerable object and an incident are detected, and this incident has an impact, then the vulnerable object is impacted by that impact.

If an incident is detected and the risk of the detection is greater than 0.8 and the confidence of the detection is less than 0.5, then the incident has priority 'Requires Verification' and a responder is assigned to identification mission.
PARKINSON: If a patient with Parkinson disease has a daily dosage plan with a specific dosage time and a missing dose event is observed, then send a notification to the doctor.

If a patient with Parkinson disease has tremor and bradykinesia of upper limb and performs a walking activity that is measured by a smart watch and a patient falling event is observed, then send a notification to the doctor.
If a patient has tremor and bradykinesia of upper limp, then that patient should be classified as a patient with Parkinson disease.
If a patient with Parkinson disease has a falling event observation and that observation happened after dosing, then send a notification alert to the doctor.
If a patient with Parkinson disease has  tremor and that tremor is observed after a dosage time then a notification is sent to the relatives and a missing dose event observation is recognized.

If a patient with Parkinson disease has bradykinesia of the upper limb and this observation  is made after dosing, then send a  notification to relatives and a missing dosing event observation is identified.
If a falling event observation is identified for a patient with Parkinson disease, then send a notification alert to the nurse and the relative.

If a person is monitored and the low-level events of tremor and  bradykinesia of the upper limb are identified, and this person has a medical prescription that contains Dopamine, then it is most likely to be a patient with Parkinson disease.
If a missing dosing event has been observed for a patient with Parkinson disease more than 2 times, then send notification to the doctor for action.

If a patient with Parkinson disease has a dose plan every 4 hours, and tremor and bradykinesia of the upper limb is identified within the boundaries of this interval then send notification to the doctor for action.

AUTOMATION: If two different states are both connected to the same transition, then both are synchronous states.
If two different states are both active at the same time, then both are concurrent states.
If a state initializes a sequence and that sequence is a parent (top-level) sequence, then the state is an initial state.
If a state finalizes a sequence and that sequence is a parent sequence, then the state is a final state.
If a state is active, then it is the current state.
If a current state has a next state, then that state is a next state.
If a sequence is initialized by an initial state and finalized by a different final state, then the sequence is a parent sequence
If a sequence is finalized by one state whose next state is the (different) state that initializes the same sequence, then the sequence is a loop.

If a transition leads from exactly one state to one other state (the source is connected to the transition, the transition to the target, and the target is the source's next state), then it is a one-to-one transition.
If one state is connected to a transition that is connected to two different next states, then the transition is a one-to-many transition.

If two different (source) states are connected to a transition that is connected to one common next state, and each (source) state has the common state as next state, then the transition is a many-to-one transition (a join)

If two different (source) states are connected to a transition which is connected to two different target states, and each source has both targets as next states, then the transition is a many-to-many transition.
If a state feeds two different transitions, and each of those transitions is also connected by another, distinct state, then the first state is a resource-shared state.
If a function is the state function of a state, then it is a state function.
If a function is the transition function of a transition, then it is a transition function.
If a function calls a service, then it is a request function.
If a transition's transition function returns 'true', then the transition is enabled
If a variable has data type 'boolean', then it is a digital variable.
If a variable has data type 'integer', then it is an analog variable.
If a variable has data type 'long', then it is an analog variable.
If a variable has data type 'float', then it is an analog variable.
If a variable has data type 'double', then it is an analog variable.
If a variable has data type 'string', then it is data.
If a variable has data type 'array', then it is data.
If a variable monitors an object, then it is an input.
If a variable acts over an object, then it is an output.
If a data item's transmitter identifier equals an actor's identifier, then that actor generates the data.
If a data item's receiver identifier equals an actor's identifier, then that actor receives the data.
If two agents have the same identifier, then they are the same individual.
If two services have the same URI, then they are the same individual.
If an agent belongs to architecture layer 1, then it is a Thing.
If an agent belongs to architecture layer 2, then it is a Device.
If an agent belongs to an architecture layer from 3 to 5 (inclusive), then it is a Software Resource.
If an agent has the feature 'Thing', then it is a Thing.
If an agent has the feature 'Device', then it is a Device.
If an agent has the feature 'Robot', then it is a Robot.
If an agent has the feature 'SoftwareResource', then it is a Software Resource.
If an agent supports both TCP and OPC UA, then its interoperability degree is High.
If an agent supports TCP and another protocol that is not OPC UA, then its interoperability degree is Medium.
If an agent supports OPC UA and another protocol that is not TCP, then its interoperability degree is Medium.
If an agent supports one protocol that is not TCP and a different protocol that is not OPC UA, then its interoperability degree is Low.
If a standard concerns content containing 'Thing', then it standardizes every 'Thing'.
If a standard concerns content containing 'Device', then it standardizes every 'Device'.
If a standard concerns content containing 'Robot', then it standardizes every 'Robot'.
If a standard concerns content containing 'SoftwareResource', then it standardizes every 'Software Resource'.
If a standard has an empty official resource, an empty DBpedia resource but an  non-empty software content, then its embedding capability is Low.
If a standard has an empty official resource, an empty DBpedia resource and empty software content, then its embedding capability is None.
If a standard has an empty official resource and an empty DBpedia resource, but non-empty software content, then its embedding capability is Low.
If a standard has an empty official resource and empty software content, but a non-empty DBpedia resource, then its embedding capability is Low.
If a standard has an empty DBpedia resource and empty software content, but a non-empty official resource, then its embedding capability is Low.
If a standard has an empty official resource, but a non-empty DBpedia resource and non-empty software content, then its embedding capability is Medium.
If a standard has an empty DBpedia resource, but a non-empty official resource and non-empty software content, then its embedding capability is Medium.
If a standard has empty software content, but a non-empty official resource and a non-empty DBpedia resource, then its embedding capability is Medium.
If a standard has a non-empty official resource, a non-empty DBpedia resource and non-empty software content, then its embedding capability is High.
